layers.authority: Chuuk State Government (permit issued by licensed diving shops)
layers.process: Divers on the Japanese wrecks in Chuuk (Truk) Lagoon first get a permit from the manager of a licensed diving shop in the state, and go with a certified dive guide from a licensed shop. The shop collects US$30 per permit (about A$43 at A$1 = USD 0.7040, RBA 30 Oct 2026) for the Chuuk Lagoon State Monument. Source is the Chuuk State Code, Title 25, Chapter 8, section 1705; the FSM law site labels this text a draft, so confirm the amount with the shop or the state.

For a Chuuk State research permit, the national archives office lists a request letter, research proposal or plan and memorandum of understanding with the state. Its page also lists national immigration documentation for non-FSM and non-US citizens. Confirm the current process and how it interacts with national NACH approval before travel.

laws.rule: The Japanese ships, aircraft and other objects sunk in Chuuk (Truk) Lagoon before 31 December 1945 are a state monument. Removing, damaging or destroying wrecks without the Governor's written permission is an offence, with a fine up to US$1,000 (about A$1,420), up to six months in jail, or both.
